speaker: Doctor
text:
I understand you have chronic bladder discomfort and frequent urination. To begin my evaluation, have you noticed any pain or burning during urination, and have you experienced fever or chills recently?

REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis
REQUEST TEST: Urine_Culture

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Urinalysis: Color Clear, pH 6.7, Specific_Gravity 1.010, Protein 1+, Glucose Negative, Ketones Negative, Blood Negative, Nitrite Negative, Leukocyte Esterase Negative, WBC 0/hpf, Squamous Epithelial Cells 2/hpf, Bacteria None; Urine_Culture: Not performed.

speaker: Patient
text: 40-year-old female. The patient reports a 5-month history of worsening bladder discomfort, which is relieved by voiding. She mentions an increased frequency of urination, voiding 10–15 times during the day and waking up 2–3 times at night to void. She denies any involuntary loss of urine. Attempts to manage the discomfort with reduced fluid intake and NSAIDs have provided minimal relief. She also reports recent painful intercourse.

speaker: Patient
text: ul intercourse. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Urinary tract infection and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is helpful; given the suspicion of a urinary tract infection, can you tell me if you have noticed any blood in your urine or if the discomfort has radiated to your back? I also need to review the results of the Urinalysis and Urine Culture you had done.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Significant for bipolar disorder, currently managed with lithium. Social history: Married and sexually active with her husband. No significant alcohol, tobacco, or recreational drug use.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Lithium-induced nephrogenic diabetes insipidus with secondary urinary tract infection.
